intro: A Seattle street musician with a National steel guitar.
story: Baby Gramps, born in Miami and a Seattle fixture, had been performing since 1964 when he played Pickathon in 2002. His first guitar was a National steel his father played in the 1930s, and his CD Same Ol' Timeously had come out in 2000. A trio CD, Hossradish, followed in 2003, and he later sang on the Rogue's Gallery pirate-ballads collection.

intro: A Seattle circus and cabaret troupe.
story: Circus Contraption, a Seattle one-ring circus and dark cabaret troupe founded in 1998, brought its band to Pickathon in 2002, the year of its CD Gallimaufry. Kevin Hinshaw led the music, and The Stranger ranked the troupe among the best of the new cabaret movement for its look, its physical skill and its musicianship. It disbanded in 2009 and issued The Show to End All Shows in 2010.

act: Dirk Powell, Courtney Granger & the Cajun Crew
intro: A Kentucky-raised multi-instrumentalist with a Cajun band.
story: Dirk Powell, who learned banjo and fiddle from his Kentucky grandfather and won the Mulate's Accordion Contest in 1994, brought a Cajun lineup with fiddler Courtney Granger to Pickathon in 2002. He went on to work with T-Bone Burnett on the Cold Mountain score. Wake, his first album since 2020, came out April 17, 2026 and includes a track called "Joyful Noise (for Courtney)."

Foghorn Stringband played Pickathon in 2002, the first of eight visits through 2016. From 2009 to 2011 it ran as a full string band, with Patrick Lind and Peter Leone beside Caleb Klauder and Nadine Landry, and Reeb Willms joined in 2011. Outshine the Sun came out in 2012 and Devil in the Seat in 2015, and the band now plays more than 300 dates a year.

intro: A Portland bluegrass and string band.
story: Harebrained, a bluegrass and string band, played Pickathon every year from 1999 to 2002.

intro: An Irish fiddle master and a Portland songwriter.
story: Kevin Burke, the London-born Bothy Band fiddler, had lived in Portland for two decades and made the 1982 album Portland with Mícheál Ó Domhnaill when he paired with songwriter Casey Neill for Pickathon in 2002. That September he went to Washington to receive a National Heritage Fellowship, one of only a handful of Irish performers chosen. He cofounded Patrick Street, toured with the Celtic Fiddle Festival, and won Ireland's Gradam Ceoil in 2016.

act: Laurie Lewis, Tom Rozum, and Tom Sauber
intro: A Berkeley bluegrass singer and fiddler with her longtime duet partner.
story: Laurie Lewis, who founded the Grant Street String Band in 1979 and was the IBMA's female vocalist of the year in 1992 and 1994, brought Tom Rozum and Tom Sauber to Pickathon in 2001 and 2002. Her duet album with Rozum, The Oak and the Laurel, had been nominated for a Grammy. She renamed her band the Right Hands in 2006, and in 2024 the IBMA gave her its Distinguished Achievement Award.
Sam Hill, a bluegrass band, played Pickathon in 2001 and 2002.
Spigot, an indie rock band, played Pickathon in 2002 and again in 2004.

Terry Robb was already a cornerstone of Portland blues in 2002, with the Muddy Award for acoustic guitar every year since 1992 and the album Stop This World behind him. After 2011 the Cascade Blues Association put his name on that award, gave him its Lifetime Achievement award in 2017, and the Oregon Music Hall of Fame inducted him. Howlin' Waters, on New Folk Records, came out in January 2026.

intro: A banjo player and former Bad Livers frontman.
story: Danny Barnes, the former Bad Livers frontman, brought his own band to Pickathon in 2002, the first of eight visits through 2018. He played every year from 2002 to 2007.

intro: A banjo champion turned slide guitarist.
story: Tony Furtado won the National Bluegrass Banjo Championship in Winfield, Kansas, in 1987, then toured with Laurie Lewis and Grant Street, and Rounder released his debut Swamped in 1990. By Pickathon 2002 he had turned toward slide guitar and songwriting, after six years in Boulder. He later made a duet album with Dirk Powell, and The Absolute Sound called his pandemic-era Decembering one of the deepest in his catalog.
